input.brief: A fictional SaaS workspace for independent studios, demonstrating its interface and sample data as an interactive product.

direction.name: The well-kept board
direction.idea: The whole page is a board of tiles fitted edge to edge with narrow gaps, like a tidy desk seen from above. Each tile is one thing: the name, a statement, a photograph, a number, a link, a short list. There is no hero and no sequence of bands; the page is one continuous composition that the eye roams. It suits subjects with many small true things to show (a studio with work, writing, clients and news; a product with several distinct capabilities) and it replaces the generic bento by having real content in every tile and a strict system for sizes.
direction.composition: A 12-column grid with 8px gaps and 8–12px outer margins, filled completely, no empty cells. Tiles use only four sizes (for example 6×4, 6×2, 3×2, 3×4 in column × row units of about 90px). Every tile is a flat filled rectangle: ground colour one step from the page, or a palette colour, or a photograph covering it. One radius everywhere (0, or 6–10px). The first screen contains: a name tile (the name at display size, the largest type on the page) with the wordmark set large, a statement tile with the description at 28–40px, two or three image tiles and one action tile in the accent colour. Text inside tiles is top-left aligned with 20–24px padding and never centred. Below the first screen the board continues with the same sizes; the last row is the footer made of tiles.
direction.typography: One grotesk in two weights. Inside tiles: a large size for single statements, a small size for lists. No uppercase labels in tile corners.
direction.colour: Page ground, tile ground one step lighter or darker, and one or two palette colours on selected tiles. Photographs supply the rest.
direction.imagery: Photographs fill whole tiles with `object-fit: cover`; choose images that crop well to both wide and tall tiles.
direction.richness: The fit. A full board with consistent gaps and varied tile contents is satisfying in the way a packed suitcase is.
direction.pitfalls: Tiles are filled, never outlined, and never carry shadows. Do not put an icon and a two-line feature blurb in every tile; vary what tiles hold. Decide the phone layout as its own board: two columns, tiles re-ordered so the name and statement lead.

hero.name: Two-by-two board
hero.blueprint: A board with 8px outer margins and 8px gaps throughout; every tile is a filled rectangle with one shared radius (0 or 8px). A 60px top row is itself made of tiles: a square ink tile with the logo mark, a wide ground-tone tile holding four text links that begin at the centre line, and an ink tile at the right end holding the single action. Below it the rest of the viewport is a two-by-two grid. Top-left: a paper tile with the name, or its first word, at clamp(96px, 12.5vw, 190px), medium weight, tracking -0.05em, sitting bottom-left on 24px padding. Top-right and bottom-left: photographs covering their tiles (object-fit: cover), both greyscale so they read as one picture continued across the board. Bottom-right is divided into two tiles side by side: a dark tile with one sentence at 24px, top-left aligned, and a tile in the accent colour with a second short statement at 24px, also top-left. Text never centres inside a tile. No tile is empty and none is outlined.
hero.mobile: The board becomes one column of tiles with 6px gaps: a top row with the logo tile and a menu tile; the name tile at 30% of the screen height with the name at 22vw bottom-left; one photograph tile at 4:3; then the dark tile and the accent tile side by side as two squares. The second photograph moves below the first screen.
hero.headline: The name, or its first word, up to 8 characters at 12.5vw; the two 24px statements are one sentence each.

type.note: A grotesk with slightly geometric bowls, set bold and very large against plain 16px text with nothing in between. Suits studios, type and product launches, and finance or tech brands that lead with the name.

palette.name: Soot and lime
palette.note: A soot-black opening and close bracket white middle sections, all in black, white and grey. Pale lime is the single action colour: every button, and at most one headline set in it on the dark ground.

photos.title: Architecture
photos.note: structure, lines, bridges, facades and building interiors

White arched bridge spanning grey water under a pale sky

motion.name: Shutter image
motion.description: The one hero or showcase image opens from an edge with a clip-path over about 1.1 seconds while the picture inside settles from 1.12 scale to rest. Use it once, on the image that matters most; later images simply are there. Recipe: 'Image shutter' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Close-ups on a board
sections.blueprint: A board of filled tiles, each a macro view of one small part of the interface. A 12-column grid with 8px gaps, 104px rows and 10px outer margins, no empty cells, no outlines. Eight tiles in four sizes: 6×4, 6×2, 3×4 and 3×2 (columns × rows). Each tile is a flat palette colour with overflow: hidden and holds one real element, built in em and enlarged to 300–400% through the font-size of its data-ui root: a toggle, a pair of key caps, a status word on its block, one figure from a readout, a slider thumb on its track, three stacked initials discs. The element is pushed off-centre so two of the tile's edges crop it. Bottom-left in every tile, 20px in: the capability's name at 18px medium and one line at 15px. One 6×2 tile holds only the heading, two to four words at clamp(36px, 4vw, 60px), top-left.
sections.mobile: Two columns, 6px gaps, rows of 28vw. Large tiles span both columns and three rows; the rest are one column by two rows. The heading tile leads at full width, two rows tall, type at 9vw. Enlarged elements keep their scale and are cropped harder; captions stay bottom-left at 16px and 14px.

sections.name: Rows as a board
sections.blueprint: The product's main list is set like a station departure board. Eight to ten real rows (transactions, issues, deploys, bookings) run the full viewport width inside 12px side margins. Each row is a filled band 72px tall, one tone off a dark ground, separated from the next by a 4px gap and never by a line; the whole board is one fragment marked data-ui. Text inside is 26–30px: the name from column 1, two or three facts at columns 6, 8 and 10, and at column 12 a status word on a solid block of its status colour; figures use tabular numerals. The section's top and bottom edges cut the first and last rows in half, so the list seems to continue. The fourth row is open: 216px tall, in the accent colour, with its detail in two lines at 17px. Clicking another row opens that one instead. No heading: the open row's name is the largest type.
sections.mobile: Rows keep the 4px gaps and are 64px tall inside 8px margins: the name at 20px on the left, the status block on the right, the other facts dropped. The open row is 200px tall and lists the dropped facts as three lines at 16px. Six rows show; the first and last are cropped.

sections.name: Plans that step up
sections.blueprint: Three plans as flat colour tiles whose heights step like a bar chart, so the bigger plan is literally bigger. The tiles sit in one row with 8px gaps, bottoms on a common base line, each 4 columns wide: the first 360px tall, the second 480px, the third 600px. Each has its own palette colour, no border and one shared radius. Inside, top-left with 28px padding: the plan name at 28px bold, the price at 56px beneath it, then what is included as plain lines at 17px (the taller tiles simply have room for more lines). The bottom 64px of every tile is a strip in a darker flat tone of that tile's colour, and the whole strip is the button with its label left-aligned. A heading of two to four words at about 4vw occupies the empty space above the two shorter tiles, top-left.
sections.mobile: Tiles stack full width in rising order, each as tall as its content, keeping its colour and its darker button strip along the bottom. Gaps of 8px. The heading leads at 9vw on two lines, and prices drop to 44px.

sections.name: A band per question
sections.blueprint: Each question owns a full-bleed band, and the bands alternate between two flat tones (ground and one step away, or two palette colours with their assigned inks) and butt together with no gap. Inside every band the same grid applies: the question in columns 1–5 at 28–32px bold, top-aligned with 56px of padding above; the answer in columns 7–12 at 18px with leading 1.5, the same padding, and 56px below. Bands are as tall as their content, so their heights differ, which gives the stack its rhythm. Four to seven bands. The heading is the first band: two to four words at about 7vw on the accent colour, flush left, taller than the rest at about 40svh with the words anchored to its bottom-left. All answers are visible; there are no toggles.
sections.mobile: Bands stay full-bleed and alternate. Inside each, the question at 22px then the answer at 17px, with 32px padding top and bottom and 20px at the sides. The heading band is 30svh tall with its words at 13vw at the bottom-left.

sections.name: The action tile
sections.blueprint: The close is one row of the board. Three filled tiles sit side by side with 8–14px gaps, all 360px tall and sharing one radius: a wide centre tile spanning columns 3–10 in the accent colour, flanked by two narrow tiles (columns 1–2 and 11–12) that run off the left and right viewport edges, as if the row had been cropped from a longer one. The centre tile holds, left-aligned and vertically centred with 40px padding: a heading of three to five words at 40px, two lines at 17px, and the action. The action is either one rectangular button or an email field 420px wide in the paper colour with the submit button nested inside its right end. The flanking tiles hold no text: one is a photograph covering the tile, the other a flat palette colour. No shadows, no outlines.
sections.mobile: The accent tile runs full width, about 300px tall, heading at 28px, field and button stacked at full width. The two flanking tiles follow beneath as a pair, each half width and 120px tall, with the same gap and the same radius.

references.name: Aspen Search
references.idea: The page is a ruled tile system with no margins: the two-word name is split across cells that alternate type, dithered canvas, black and one mint green.
references.hero: A 60px top bar ruled into cells: black logo square, local time, nav links starting at the centre line, a theme toggle and a black contact cell flush right. Below, the viewport is a two-by-two grid divided by 1px black lines, no outer margin. Top-left is white with the first word of the name at 12.5vw, weight 450, sitting bottom-left. Top-right and bottom-left cells hold a black-and-white dithered canvas crossed by large pale-grey blade shapes that ignore cell borders. The bottom-right quadrant splits into a black cell (24px white summary, mono caps action row at its base) and a mint cell (second statement, client-logo marquee along the bottom).
references.type: Suisse Intl at weight 450 for everything, tracking about -0.02em; Suisse Intl Mono in small caps for actions, bullet lists and footer. Wordmark 180px against 24px statements and 16px body. Later headings switch to all caps at about 9vw with leading near 0.9.
references.colour: #ffffff #232323 #d9d9d9 #a1ffcb #969797 — White, near-black and two greys fill the cells; a single mint green floods whole tiles (a statement, a stat, the closing call to action) as the only colour. Cool and flat.
references.imagery: A canvas of 1-bit ordered-dither dots with soft tonal blobs, overlaid with flat pale-grey shards taken from the logo; services get white wireframe line drawings of spheres. No photography anywhere.
references.layout: Zero page margin: everything is edge-to-edge cells on a two-column grid with halves subdivided, separated by 1px rules. Sections differ only by cell fill and cell height. Type always sits top-left or bottom-left in its cell with about 20px padding; some cells are left deliberately empty.

sections.description: The second screen continues the hero grid: a black cell carries a two-line all-caps slogan at about 9vw set hard against its left edge; a light grey cell top-right holds the second word of the name at the same giant size as the first, bottom-aligned; dither canvas fills the rest. Then a white row where the left half is empty and a 24px long-form text runs only in the right column.

Stair-stepped tiles instead of a row. A tall mint cell fills the left half with one figure at about 5vw in its top-left corner and nothing else. On the right, a shorter black tile starts higher with a white figure top-left and a small caption at its bottom edge; a grey tile sits to its right, stepped down, same internal layout. The tiles' unequal heights leave white notches.

Left half: a light grey cell with a three-line all-caps heading whose middle line is pushed to the right edge, a small paragraph low in the cell and a black mono-caps button bottom-right. Right half: black, split by hairlines into stacked rows; each row has a tiny mono index, a 28px title, a short paragraph in a second column, a white wireframe drawing and a mono caps list with small mint square bullets.

A grid of cells: white cell with a short statement top-left; a cell with a plain nav list; a cell with two small analogue clock icons and city times; a hairline row with email left and a social link right. Below, a black cell with the logo and lowercase wordmark centred large, beside a mint cell with a heading top-left and a thin diagonal arrow drawn into its bottom-right corner.

steal: Rule the whole viewport into cells with 1px lines and no page margin, then give the nav, the headline, the summary and the proof each its own cell with a flat fill.
Split a two-word brand name across two cells on consecutive screens at the same giant size, so scrolling completes the name.
Use a 1-bit ordered-dither texture as the picture in otherwise empty cells and let large flat logo fragments cross the cell borders to tie the grid together.
references.media: One halftone canvas of the brand mark is seen only through chosen cells of the tile grid, about half the hero area, and returns in sticky half panels and as a full-bleed canvas behind knockout words. Portraits are high-key black and white in a staggered row with offset heights, client logos keep their brand colours inside their own tiles, and there is no video and no rounded corner anywhere.
references.motion: A dark screen gives way at about 1.2s to a small mark on a 20s coin spin, the white grid arrives by 2.5s with the name rising through a mask, and the dither resolves by 4.5s. Lenis drives CSS sticky stacking (12 sticky elements, no pins): hero rows slide over each other and stat tiles lock under the header one by one; text fades in by line over 1000ms cubic-bezier(0.23,1,0.32,1) in 100ms steps (193 WAAPI calls), and a theme toggle wipes the page with a 1.2s clip-path sweep.

references.name: Justin Lerner
references.idea: The portfolio is a hairline grid of square cells in which the letters of the owner's name are scattered among small animated project emblems, so name and work form one crossword-like board.
references.hero: White page divided by pale grey hairlines into five columns of exact squares (each 20vw), so three full rows and a sliver of a fourth show. No header, navigation or text block. Each cell holds one centred object about half the cell wide: either a single black slab-serif capital at 5.6vw (one in the top-left cell, one top-right, three more scattered through rows two and three) or a small project emblem such as a pixel speech bubble, a photographed bowl, a red robot arm, a wireframe figure, a logo badge or a line-drawn building. One cell holds only a soft blurred cloud. About 90% of the area is white.
references.type: Museo Slab is the only face on desktop: weight-500 capitals at 80px used as grid letters, with no body copy at all (eleven words on the page). Mobile adds light italic slab project names and small sans year tabs.
references.colour: #ffffff #e9eae8 #111111 #fff200 #f0563a #4fd0c8 — White ground, grey hairlines, black letters. Colour arrives only in the emblems, each in its own one- or two-colour scheme (yellow, coral, teal, purple). Mobile adds two solid yellow icon tiles.
references.imagery: Small spot illustrations and logos in deliberately mixed styles (pixel art, line drawing, isometric, wireframe mesh, one cut-out photo), each centred in a square cell with no frame or background, and animated.
references.layout: A single edge-to-edge grid of 20vw squares with hairline dividers and no outer margin; the whole site is about 1.3 screens. Mobile switches to two columns and adds a year tab in each cell's top-right corner and an italic name under each emblem.

sections.description: The grid continues for one more row below the fold with five cells holding only emblems. Across frames the emblems are caught in different states: a logo badge collapsing to a small monogram, a scan line moving down the wireframe figure, a pencil travelling across a drawn face, a coin appearing and disappearing. Each cell is a tiny looping or hover-driven animation, with no captions on desktop.

Mobile header built from the same cells: a small square with the initial on crosshair lines at left, an empty cell, then two solid-yellow square tiles carrying a document icon and a paper-plane icon. Below, the two-column grid gives each project a boxed year tab notched into the top-right corner of its cell and an italic slab project name near the bottom, sometimes overlapping the emblem.

steal: Spell the name by dropping its letters into scattered cells of a hairline grid and fill the remaining cells with project marks, so identity and index share one structure.
Give each project a single small animated emblem centred in a large empty square instead of a screenshot thumbnail.
On mobile, notch a small boxed year tab into the corner of each grid cell and label the cell with an italic name at its base.

references.name: Rows
references.idea: Radical understatement: a product about simple lists is sold with a 27px headline, 12px copy and a column of small live demos, each proving one interaction.
references.hero: Warm off-white page, almost empty. Everything hangs on one vertical line 27% in from the left. A small striped-letter logo mark sits there near the top; 220px lower comes a two-line headline at only 27px (under 2vw), then three lines of 13px body about 370px wide, then a near-black rectangular button with 4px corners beside a text link with an arrow. A single grey sign-in link sits in the top-right corner; there is no navigation bar. More than 80% of the viewport is blank. At the bottom edge the first feature module peeks in: grey demo panel left, short text column right.
references.type: Suisse Intl only, weight 450–500, tracking −0.04em. Headline 27px, feature headings about 16px on two lines, body 12px. Three sizes in total, no uppercase and no display moment; hierarchy comes from weight and empty space alone.
references.colour: #f5f6f1 #e6e7e1 #1a191d #ffffff #c7372f #3aa56a — Warm paper off-white with slightly darker grey-green demo panels and near-black type; colour appears only inside the UI as priority dots, outlined status pills and one green or red action button.
references.imagery: No pictures: small live-rendered fragments of the app (two or three white list rows with dots, status pills, avatars and a visible cursor) sit in flat grey panels of fixed 368px width with barely rounded corners.
references.layout: One content block about 650px wide, offset left of centre, repeated down the page: 368px demo panel plus a 245px text column, top-aligned, separated by 200px or more of empty space. The logo mark sticks to the top-left corner on scroll. Footer is one line.

sections.description: The repeating module: a flat grey panel roughly 368px wide and 120–190px tall holding a tiny mock list (white rows with 6px radius, a coloured numbered dot at left, task title, an outlined status pill, an avatar, a chevron) and often a cursor mid-action. To its right, 20px away and top-aligned, a medium-weight heading of one or two lines and two short paragraphs at 11–12px in a column only 245px wide. Modules never alternate sides; they stack with large gaps.

The closing block keeps the same narrow measure: a three-line paragraph at 13px, then the identical button and arrow-link pair from the hero, left-aligned on the text column's axis. After a long gap a single hairline spans the 650px block and under it sits one row of tiny footer text: brand line at left, six links and a copyright strung along the right.

steal: Set the headline at near-body size (under 2vw) and let empty space, not scale, give it importance.
Explain each feature with a tiny cropped fragment of real UI in a fixed-width flat panel, one interaction per panel, with the cursor left visible.
Hang the whole page on one off-centre left edge and never break it, logo and footer included.
